land.text: Yemen, where the last Ayyubid al-Malik al-Mas'ud 'left Yemen in 1229' and handed governance to his commander

predecessors.note: The page's infobox says 'Preceded by' the Ayyubid dynasty and 'Established: 1229'. The text dates the proclamation of independent rule to 1235, after a diploma of recognition from the Abbasid caliph al-Mustansir I; Cliopatria's row starts in 1236.

land.text: the Tihama lowland and the southern highlands, with Aden

successors.note: Tahirid page: infobox 'Established: 1454', 'Preceded by: Rasulid dynasty'; the Rasulid sultan al-Mas'ud 'gave up his throne in favour of az-Zafir Amir bin Tahir' in 1454 (Rasulid page). The Tahirids 'ruled in the first place in the Tihama lowland and the southern highlands'. Cliopatria's Tahirid row starts in 1459.

land.text: Shihr in Hadramawt, taken by the Tahirids in 1457 and lost 'at the end of the fifteenth century to the Kathiri princedom' (Tahirid page)

successors.note: Listed as a successor in the Rasulid infobox ('Succeeded by: Tahirid Sultanate, Kathiri Sultanate'), but only at the end of the 15th century on the Tahirid page, not in 1454. The Kathiri have no Cliopatria row and no dossier yet.

capitals.name: Zabid
capitals.note: Infobox 'Capital: Zabid'; 'The coastal capital was established in Zabid'. The page adds that the mountain city of Taiz (13.61 N, 44.04 E) 'became the base of the dynasty together with Zabid' under al-Muzaffar Yusuf I (1249-1295), with no year; the Tahirid page calls Zabid their winter capital.

rulers.name: al-Mansur Umar I
rulers.note: Table of Rasulid rulers; Umar is 'Umar ibn Ali' in the page's text.

rulers.name: al-Mujahid Ali
rulers.note: Captured by Egyptian Mamluks at Mecca in 1350 (text).

rulers.name: az-Zahir Yahya
rulers.note: The table gives 1428-1439; the family tree on the same page gives 1428-1438.

rulers.name: al-Mas'ud Abu al-Qasim
rulers.note: Gave up the throne to az-Zafir Amir bin Tahir in 1454 and withdrew to Mecca.

correction.text: 1229-1235: Umar's Yemen, drawn as Cliopatria's 1236 shape

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for the years before Cliopatria's row: infobox 'Established: 1229'; 'The last Ayyubid, al-Malik al-Mas'ud, left Yemen in 1229' and entrusted governance to an ambitious member of his mercenary force; Umar 'proclaimed himself ruler in his own right in 1235 after receiving a diploma of recognition' from the caliph. The page gives no extent for these years.

correction.text: the Tihama lowland and the southern highlands, with Zabid, Taiz, Sanaa and Aden and the south coast 'up to Dhofar' loosely held; shape unchanged, but it holds for 1236-1323 only

keyframe_review.note: Matches the page: Yusuf I 'confirmed Rasulid rule over the Tihamah lowland and the southern highlands', Sanaa was 'temporarily occupied' under him, and 'the southern coast of Arabia up to Dhofar was kept under loose control'. The shape (377,950 km2, bbox 42.2-52.4 E, 12.6-19.3 N) contains Zabid, Taiz, Aden, Sanaa and Shihr and excludes Mecca and Salalah. The infobox gives no area to compare. Years cut at 1323 because Sanaa falls in 1324.

minus.text: Sanaa, 'temporarily occupied' under Yusuf I and taken by the Zaidi forces in 1324

correction.text: 1324-1442: the Rasulid shape without Sanaa, which the Zaidi forces took in 1324

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 'Zaidi forces took Sanaa in 1324'; the Zaydi imams 'regained ground in the highlands from the late 13th century'. The page does not give the northern limit that followed; Sanaa with a 30 km radius is the researcher's minimal cut. The Zaydi territory beyond Sanaa is the neighbouring imams' (the page names no other town).

minus.text: Sanaa, 'temporarily occupied' under Yusuf I and taken by the Zaidi forces in 1324

correction.text: 1443-1452: without Sanaa and without Lahij, which fell to the Tahir clan in 1443

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 'Lahij fell to the Tahir clan in 1443, followed by Aden in 1454'.

minus.text: Sanaa, 'temporarily occupied' under Yusuf I and taken by the Zaidi forces in 1324

correction.text: 1453: the realm without Sanaa and Lahij, still with Aden; the dynasty ends in 1454

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria draws the Rasulids to 1458, but the page's infobox ends the dynasty in 1454 ('gave up his throne in favour of az-Zafir Amir bin Tahir'); the Tahirid page has 'Established: 1454'. Cliopatria's 1454-1458 years belong to the Tahirids (its Tahirid row starts in 1459). The shape holds for 1453 only.

region.text: Yemen under Umar, the last Ayyubid's commander

ledger.note: 1229: Umar takes over the government of Yemen when the last Ayyubid al-Mas'ud leaves, the start of the Rasulid dynasty. Infobox 'Established: 1229'; 'The last Ayyubid, al-Malik al-Mas'ud, left Yemen in 1229'. The text dates his proclamation as independent ruler to 1235 (after the Abbasid caliph's diploma), so 1229-1235 is the researcher's reading of the infobox year; the ayyubid-sultanate dossier records Yemen's loss in 1229.

1238: the Rasulids hold Mecca (bridging). The page says only that 'the Rasulids temporarily held control over the holy city of Mecca', with no year; 1238 is the year the ayyubid-sultanate dossier records for Nur al-Din Umar's capture of Mecca (from the Ayyubid dynasty page, not opened here), so the year needs a page. [Reviewer me-09-d, 2026-10-24] Year now sourced: the Ayyubid dynasty page says the Rasulids moved 'to end Ayyubid suzerainty in the Hejaz, which they accomplished in 1238 when Nur al-Din Umar captured Mecca'. Confidence raised from 1 to 2 (place and year on the page; how long Mecca stayed Rasulid is still open), source changed from Rasulid_dynasty.

region.text: Sanaa, 'temporarily occupied' under Yusuf I and taken by the Zaidi forces in 1324

ledger.note: 1324: the Zaydi imams take Sanaa. 'Zaidi forces took Sanaa in 1324'; under Yusuf I (1249-1295) the sultan had 'temporarily occupied' it and defeated the imams several times. When the Rasulids first took Sanaa is not dated on the page. The Cliopatria row 'Imamate of Yemen' covers only 1814-1872 under the same Wikipedia article ('Imams of Yemen').

1350: Mecca passes out of Rasulid reach (bridging). 'In 1350 the Rasulid sultan al-Mujahid Ali was captured by Egyptian Mamluks in Mecca when he went on a pilgrimage'; the page also says 'The Hijaz itself fell to the Mamluk Sultanate of Egypt' without a year. Treating the capture as the end of any Rasulid hold on Mecca is the researcher's judgment.
1443: Lahij falls to the Tahir clan. 'Lahij fell to the Tahir clan in 1443, followed by Aden in 1454.' The Tahirid page agrees: 'Lahij, north of Aden, was taken over by them in 1443.'
1454: the Tahirids take Aden. 'Followed by Aden in 1454'; Tahirid page: 'the important port of Aden was swiftly taken by the brothers Amir and Ali bin Tahir'.

region.text: the remaining realm: the Tihama lowland and southern highlands, with Aden

ledger.note: 1454: the last Rasulid sultan gives up the throne to the Tahirids and the dynasty ends. Tahirid page infobox 'Established: 1454', 'Preceded by: Rasulid dynasty'; al-Mas'ud 'gave up his throne in favour of az-Zafir Amir bin Tahir' and 'withdrew to Mecca in the same year'. Cliopatria carries the Rasulids to 1458; the Tahirid page also has Shihr taken in 1457.

wars.name: Rasulid-Zaydi struggle for Sanaa and the highlands

zones.text: Sanaa, 'temporarily occupied' under Yusuf I and taken by the Zaidi forces in 1324

wars.outcome: Under Yusuf I the Rasulids 'temporarily occupied' Sanaa and defeated the imams several times; the Zaidis regained ground in the highlands from the late 13th century and took Sanaa in 1324.
wars.note: The page names no war and dates no campaign: 'from' is the start of Yusuf I's reign (bridging), 'to' the 1324 fall of Sanaa. No contest events are written because no campaign is dated.

wars.name: Capture of al-Mujahid Ali at Mecca
wars.outcome: 'In 1350 the Rasulid sultan al-Mujahid Ali was captured by Egyptian Mamluks in Mecca when he went on a pilgrimage.' The page says the Rasulids had 'temporarily held control' of Mecca and that the Mamluks 'tended to increase their influence in Hijaz and the holy cities'.
wars.note: Not a territorial war on the page; kept because it is the only dated Mecca event.

wars.name: Tahirid takeover of the Rasulid realm
wars.outcome: Lahij fell to the Tahir clan in 1443 and Aden in 1454; al-Mas'ud gave up the throne to az-Zafir Amir bin Tahir in 1454 and 'The new ruling clan governed Yemen from 1454 to 1517 as the Tahirids'.
wars.note: The pages give no battles or months; no contest events are written.

certainty.note: No page gives a frontier line. The Zaydi frontier in the northern highlands, the Hadramawt coast ('up to Dhofar ... under loose control') and any hold on Mecca are approximate; Cliopatria's shape is the only outline.

notes:
Cliopatria 'Rasulid Dynasty' 1236-1458, two identical shapes (1236-1452 and 1453-1458, 377,950 km2, bbox 42.2-52.4 E, 12.6-19.3 N). Two pages opened (the budget). The dates disagree: the infobox says 1229-1454 (and the Ayyubid dossier has Yemen lost in 1229), the text puts independent rule in 1235, Cliopatria 1236-1458; the dossier starts 1229 and ends 1454 (Tahirid page: 'Established: 1454'), so Cliopatria's 1454-1458 years are the Tahirids' (their row starts in 1459). Verdicts: 1236 adjust (holds to 1323), 1453 adjust (holds 1453 only); three new keyframes (1229, 1324, 1443). The shape fits the page's description of the realm (Tihama, southern highlands, coast loosely to Dhofar); it contains Sanaa and Shihr, so Sanaa (1324) and Lahij (1443) are cut out. No infobox area, so no area comparison.
Open: (1) Mecca: the page says only 'temporarily held control over the holy city'; the 1238 gain and 1350 loss are confidence-1 bridging and need a page (Ayyubid dynasty for 1238). (2) When the Rasulids took Sanaa is undated (Yusuf I's reign 1249-1295); the Cliopatria shape includes Sanaa from 1236. (3) Hadramawt/Shihr and Dhofar/Zufar ('a side-branch of the family governed for a while') are not dated or described in these pages; the Tahirid page has Shihr taken in 1457. (4) The Zaydi imams need a medieval dossier: Cliopatria's 'Imamate of Yemen' (slug imamate-of-yemen) covers 1814-1872 only, under the Wikipedia article 'Imams of Yemen'; used here as the counterpart. (5) The Kathiri Sultanate (infobox successor) has no row or dossier. (6) Taiz as co-capital has no year. (7) The Rasulid page names the founder Umar ibn Ali and lists no Rasulid-Mamluk treaty or tribute; the Mamluk conquest of the Tahirids (1516) is in the mamluk-sultanate dossier.
